story.title: Iconic Fashion Designer Bob Mackie Passes Away at 87
story.summary: Bob Mackie, the legendary fashion designer known for his extravagant costumes worn by stars like Cher, Tina Turner, and Diana Ross, has died at the age of 87. His designs, which defined Hollywood glamour for decades, left a lasting impact on American fashion.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Mackie’s work matter beyond red carpets?
explore_lenses.title: Costume as pop-cultural storytelling
explore_lenses.summary: Mackie’s importance came from treating clothing as part of a performer’s character and a televised spectacle, helping make costumes central to the public identities of stars such as Cher and Carol Burnett.

claims.text: Mackie described his outfits as costumes for characters rather than simply fashion, saying his aim was for audiences to find them interesting or wild.
The Council of Fashion Designers of America said it honored him in 2019 for his impact on American fashion and for bringing glamour to performers including Diana Ross, Carol Burnett and RuPaul.
His “Starlet O’Hara” curtain-rod gown for Carol Burnett’s 1976 parody of Gone With the Wind is held by the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History.

explore_lenses.label: How did Mackie become a star designer?
explore_lenses.title: A career built through television and collaboration
explore_lenses.summary: Mackie progressed from Hollywood sketch work to long-running television, concert and stage collaborations, creating a body of work recognized by the TV, theater and fashion industries.

claims.text: AP reports that Mackie studied illustration and costume design, worked for costume designer Edith Head, and then secured work on The Carol Burnett Show.

The Television Academy records wins for Mackie’s work on The Carol Burnett Show and The Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour, alongside nominations for productions involving Diana Ross, Cher and other entertainers.
His official biography lists nine Emmy wins, three Oscar nominations and a 2019 Tony Award for The Cher Show, evidence that his work extended across television, film and Broadway.

explore_lenses.label: What will preserve Mackie’s legacy now?
explore_lenses.title: His work is already entering an institutional afterlife
explore_lenses.summary: Mackie’s designs and sketches are already held or exhibited by cultural institutions, but the immediate arrangements following his death have not been publicly detailed in the reporting reviewed.

claims.text: The Palm Springs Art Museum presented five original gowns and costumes and selected sketches in its January–March 2026 Mackie presentation, including works associated with Cher, Diana Ross, Tina Turner and Carol Burnett.
The museum described the presentation as a focused tribute rather than a comprehensive retrospective, indicating that no single recent exhibition purported to encompass his full output.
A statement posted to Mackie’s social-media accounts said his designs would continue to bring beauty into the world; it did not announce public memorial or estate plans.

story_report.summary: Bob Mackie, the fashion designer celebrated for sequined gowns and extravagant stage costumes, has died at 87. He dressed performers including Cher, Tina Turner and Diana Ross, creating looks that became closely associated with their public personas. Mackie’s death leaves a body of work that reached television, film, Broadway and museum collections, while fashion institutions credited him with bringing glamour to generations of entertainers and shaping American fashion.

sections.heading: Bob Mackie’s Costume-Making Philosophy
sections.body: Mackie described his work as costumes for characters, rather than simply fashion. He said he wanted audiences to find the designs interesting or wild, an approach reflected in the theatrical scale of his work for performers. The Council of Fashion Designers of America honored him with its Geoffrey Beene Lifetime Achievement Award in 2019, citing his impact on American fashion and the glamour he brought to figures including Diana Ross, Carol Burnett and RuPaul.

sections.heading: Bob Mackie’s Entertainment Career
sections.body: According to the Associated Press, Mackie studied illustration and costume design, worked for costume designer Edith Head and later joined The Carol Burnett Show. Television Academy records include wins for his work on The Carol Burnett Show and The Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour, as well as nominations tied to productions involving Cher, Diana Ross and other entertainers. His official biography lists nine Emmy wins, three Oscar nominations and a 2019 Tony Award for The Cher Show.

sections.heading: Bob Mackie’s Designs in Museums
sections.body: Mackie’s work is represented in museum collections and recent exhibitions. The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History holds his “Starlet O’Hara” curtain-rod gown, created for Carol Burnett’s 1976 Gone With the Wind parody. The Palm Springs Art Museum displayed five original Mackie gowns and costumes, along with selected sketches, from January through March 2026, featuring work associated with Cher, Diana Ross, Tina Turner and Burnett; the museum described the presentation as a focused tribute, not a comprehensive retrospective.

unresolved.text: As of Sept. 14, 2026, consulted reporting had not specified Mackie’s cause of death, funeral or memorial arrangements, or plans for his remaining archive and brand.

related_stories.title: DHS Report Reveals Immigrants Confined in Small Cages at 'Alligator Alcatraz'
related_stories.summary: A report from the Department of Homeland Security's inspector general has revealed that immigrants detained at the now-closed Florida facility known as 'Alligator Alcatraz' were held in outdoor cages slightly larger than phone booths for extended periods. The findings detail the conditions faced by detainees at this facility, which has since been shuttered.

His comments come in response to a report suggesting Ottawa was considering an 'associate membership' with the bloc.

related_stories.title: EU Leaders Convene in Finland to Discuss Arctic Policy Amid Security Concerns
related_stories.summary: European leaders are gathering in Finland to address key issues related to the Arctic, including shipping routes, resource management, and security challenges posed by the increasing presence of Russia. The meeting comes as the region becomes more accessible due to melting ice, raising concerns about geopolitical tensions involving the US, China, and Russia.
